uncertainties: Whether the play-type classifier artifact (FAM:SF-PAP-096) has been fully resolved and applied to the data versions available

If many player-pair or team-context combinations are tested, false positive risk is high; multiplicity must be controlled

design.estimand: The causal effect of a teammate's DRIVE on the immediately following PNR possession's points per possession (PPP), compared to the same team's PNR PPP when the preceding possession was not a teammate DRIVE (or the overall PNR PPP baseline).
design.unit: A consecutive pair of offensive possessions for the same team (possession i and i+1), where possession i+1 is classified as a PNR and possession i is classified as a DRIVE by any teammate (excluding the PNR initiator when possible).

design.power: Simulation-based power calculation using historical PNR PPP variance and sequence frequencies; target 80% power to detect a +0.10 PPP effect at the team level, requiring an estimated 2,000 total sequences (~67 per team).
design.controls: Game period (quarter/OT), score margin bucket (e.g., -10 to -5, -5 to 5, 5 to 10, >10), possession start type (transition vs half-court), team fixed or random effects, and whether the preceding DRIVE was against set defense.
design.falsification: Test the effect of a teammate DRIVE two possessions before ('lag-2') on PNR PPP, expecting a null result. Also test effect of an opponent DRIVE preceding the team's PNR. If either shows a significant effect, the primary model may be capturing spurious correlation.
design.multiplicity: If player-pair analysis is conducted, use Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate control with a pre-registered list of interested pairs. Primary team-level test is a single hypothesis.
design.decision_rule: Pre-register α=0.05 one-sided for a positive effect. Report 95% confidence intervals. Consider the effect practically significant if the PPP increase exceeds 0.05 points per possession.
design.data_version: The play-type classifier version must be one where the assisted-flag leak has been fixed (post SF-PAP-096 resolution). Confirm by auditing label accuracy on a random sample of 500 labeled possessions.
